body: OWNER LIVE DOCS REVIEW, 2026-08-31. The owner judged /scala/getting-started/ better but still extremely thin and asked: this is a big library, what does it do? I inspected the exact docs successor now served at 127.0.0.1:8765 and found two distinct facts. First, the preview process was serving a stale dist: the source already contained 17 pages, seven executed Scala workflows, archived outputs, four source-derived static figures, and the expanded sidebar, but the visible build exposed only the earlier subset. I rebuilt the same preserved export in place without stopping the server; the full navigation is now visible. Second, /scala/getting-started/ remains intentionally only the source-atlas workflow. The actual capability answer lives on / and across model-a-story, represent-recall, align-and-interpret, summarize-recall, score-interview, embeddings, and save-and-deliver. Acceptance implication: do not mistake the stale build for missing authored content, but do preserve the owner finding at the route level. A page labeled as a start must orient the reader to the end-to-end purpose and route map before narrowing to spans, or its title/navigation must make that narrow scope unmistakable. No docs source was edited; current served bytes remain the unlanded successor, not canonical main. Calibration work remains my assigned path.
